verdict_reason: All 4 hard gates pass and no item is below 7, but the average is 7.8 (< 8). Big improvement over v1 (6.9). The two weakest items are payoff and surprise: the claim is true but the twist is soft, because once the viewer hears 'thirteen years' the result is predictable.
v1_fixes_check: All landed: hook now carries the span (since 2013); you/Benny avatar is consistent; friend gives a reason (too small); lines 2 and 4 are no longer duplicates; the 'broke/everyone' line is now two plain sentences that re-name GTA 6; the moral line is cut; A/B ending is plain; heavy-jar and cashier-counting gags added; crowd removed; timing note says present tense.

checks.math: Recomputed with .venv/Scripts/python: 2013-09-17 to 2026-11-19 = 4,811 days; x $0.02 = $96.22; minus $79.99 = $16.23; 1 cent/day = $48.11. All correct. Caveats: (a) Sept 17, 2013 is inferred, not stated on a fetched page (true in reality; the speech says only 'since 2013'); (b) $16.23 LEFT is pre-tax, so it is slightly generous (the badge reads as if after the purchase); acceptable, or write 'ABOUT $16 LEFT'. Spoken 'ninety-six' is a safe round-down.
checks.word_count: Spoken (say) words = 74 (17+5+7+6+7+5+6+5+4+8+4), inside 55-75 but one word from the cap. Estimate at am_liam 0.9 is about 30-33 s: the upper half of the window (spelled-out 'G T A six' is slow). Line 1 is 17 spoken words (14 as written); the owner allowed this and it is easy to follow, so the clarity gate is not failed for it.
checks.scenes: 11 scenes (8-12 OK). On-screen text all <= 5 words. No ph/Taglish anywhere.
checks.hype: Rides the Nov 19, 2026 release well: 'GTA 6' is named in the first 5 s and again at the twist, and 'Then GTA 6 comes out' is the release-day beat. BUT it is only true on release day: it must be posted on Nov 19 (today is Nov 17; hold it). If posted early, the Nov 19 badge and the present tense read wrong.
checks.ip: Clean. 'GTA 6' only as spoken/plain white text (no logo, lettering, colors, art), blank generic game box, plain 'STORE' sign, no Rockstar characters, footage or music. 'NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE' badge plus description note; hypothetical, no guaranteed outcome.
checks.drawability: Feasible with docs/scene-format.md (headline, counter with suffix, bubble, stamp, badge, coins, confetti, prop). Concerns: (1) scene 4 visual contains a stray authoring note ('a tiny gray-hair gag is not needed') that the video generator may take literally; (2) scene 8 stacks counting bubble + zoom-out + SMASH stamp + jar break + coins + counter into one 5-word line (about 2 s): keep to counter, stamp, coins; (3) the hooded stranger is the friend in scenes 2-6 and the cashier in scene 8, so it looks like the friend works at the store: confusing, use a second stranger or have Benny hand the jar over a plain counter; (4) 'jar prop scale up' needs a prop item with scale beats, which the format does not support; swap prop scale via two items or reuse coin rain.

fixes: Line 9 / payoff (7): the best number ($16.23 left) is on screen only. Say it: replace line 9 with 'You buy the game, with sixteen dollars left.' (+4 words), and pay for it by cutting line 7 'You carry the heavy jar inside.' (6 words, gag only, no new information) and putting the heavy-jar gag into the first 1-2 s of scene 8. Net: 72 spoken words, safer length, stronger payoff.

Lines 5-6 (surprise, 7): the friend having no money does not connect to the game or to the jar, so the twist is soft. Make it hit: 'Your friend wants GTA 6 too. He has no money.' or keep it but show him begging at the counter. The real 'wait, what?' is the result: consider holding the reveal so the viewer thinks 2 cents is too small until line 8 (the 'too small' bubble in line 3 already sets this up; a visible tiny coin in scene 2 vs the huge pile in scene 8 will make the contrast land).

Line 4 (escalation, 8): 'You keep going for thirteen years.' is the longest static beat and it only restates the hook span. Add a new element in the visual (the friend gets older or Benny gets a long beard; cash-prop gag) or let the counter end on '13 YEARS LATER' with a sudden cut so the time-jump feels like a punchline.

Line 1 (hook, 8; clarity, 8): the hook takes about 6 s to finish and 'G T A six' lands last. Keep it as the owner allowed, but put the snap-zoom on 'two cents a day' (first 1.5 s, the strongest curiosity words) and not only on 'GTA 6'. Keep letter-by-letter 'G T A' crisp (TTS may blur it); test with am_liam before rendering.

Line 10 (ending, 8): 'spend it all' is vague. 'spend it all on what?' may pull viewers to reply; use 'or spend it all today?' only if the word count allows (74 now, so cut line 7 first). Line 11 is fine and ends the moment the question is asked.

Facts (8): confirm the GTA 5 date (Sept 17, 2013) from a fetched page or keep it off screen (already the plan); change the '$16.23 LEFT' badge to 'ABOUT $16 LEFT' to avoid a tax nitpick in the comments.
Drawability: delete the stray note in the line-4 visual, simplify scene 8, and use a different character as cashier than the friend (see checks.drawability).
